explained.tdh.impl.title: Implementations and vectors
explained.tdh.impl.lede: The programs that compute TDH, which one runs when, and how to test your own implementation against the vectors and a real day.
explained.tdh.impl.toc.label: On this page
explained.tdh.impl.cast.label: The programs
explained.tdh.impl.cast.title: Two programs, each run two ways
explained.tdh.impl.cast.body: Program A, the Rust core, and program B are written separately. A validator is to run both before it signs (D125). Each also runs inside a zero-knowledge prover: proof A is program A in SP1, proof B is program B in RISC Zero.
explained.tdh.impl.cast.caption: The programs that compute TDH
explained.tdh.impl.a.name: Program A
explained.tdh.impl.a.written: Ported from the Rust reference, no rule changed
explained.tdh.impl.a.runs: Every day in the comparison; 6529.io's own computation once 6529.io cuts over to it (D132)
explained.tdh.impl.a.runsLate: Every day in the comparison; 6529.io's own computation once 6529.io cuts over to it (D132), which as of {checked} it has not
explained.tdh.impl.b.name: Program B
explained.tdh.impl.b.written: In a clean room, from the specifications and vectors only; found the flaw in the first netting rule
explained.tdh.impl.b.runs: In CI against program A; inside a validator before it signs: decided (D125), not in the daily run yet
explained.tdh.impl.python.name: Python reference
explained.tdh.impl.python.runs: Every day, from program A's input file
explained.tdh.impl.rustRef.name: Rust reference
explained.tdh.impl.rustRef.written: In a clean room from P26; listed {choices} choices, each now a rule
explained.tdh.impl.lean.name: Lean model
explained.tdh.impl.lean.runs: CI on every change: the build and its axiom audit, P26's vectors, {random} seeded random inputs and the files that are no vector. The day of {day} was replayed once, by hand.
explained.tdh.impl.live.name: 6529.io
explained.tdh.impl.live.runs: Publishes TDH today; compared every day
explained.tdh.impl.cast.note: Computing one day takes about {time} (the Rust reference, on the day of {day}); the whole run on the latest day took {runtime}, almost all of it reading Ethereum. Programs A and B will be published with the validator code (D116), no date set; the references and the Lean model are in 6529's private design record.

explained.tdh.impl.run.read: Read {params} as the registry, then {cycle}, {transfers}, {events} and {logs}.
explained.tdh.impl.run.compare: Compare every field of the {expected} blocks. {legacy} is not normative.
explained.tdh.impl.run.invalid: A vector with {invalid} passes when you reject its input; the strict run also checks the section you cite.
explained.tdh.impl.roots.label: The roots to aim for
explained.tdh.impl.roots.title: Everything that produced the day of {date}
explained.tdh.impl.roots.blockLabel: The values that pin the day of {date}
explained.tdh.impl.roots.comment: the result dated {date} (cycle {cycle}), as its file reports it
explained.tdh.impl.roots.retired: retired name; {current} from the builds' next version
explained.tdh.impl.roots.body: Hit the cycle root and the wallet root, and your records equal the day's. Miss them, and compare your records one by one with 6529.io's signed upload for that day: it lists every identity's TDH.
explained.tdh.impl.ask.label: Asked of the owner
explained.tdh.impl.ask.body: Publish one day's canonical input file. It is chain data, not code, and with it an outside implementation could reproduce a day byte for byte today, before the validator code is published.
explained.tdh.impl.rounds.label: How they were checked
explained.tdh.impl.rounds.title: {rounds} rounds of differential tests
explained.tdh.impl.rounds.body: From {from} to {to}, {rounds} rounds of generated days ran through the Lean model, the Python reference, program A and program B. Each finding was settled and pinned by a new vector but one: how deep a file may nest ({open}) is still open, and P26 sets no limit yet. In CI, every change to P26 runs {random} seeded random inputs through Lean, Python and the Rust reference.
